title: Take bigger jobs without fronting higher costs: Deposits & payment schedules with Topline Pro
summary: Add deposits and payment schedules to any Topline Pro quote. Homeowners sign and pay on one screen, so you’re not fronting material costs.
body_markdown:
## **Key Takeaways**


- Topline Pro now helps you **collect deposits and ongoing milestone payments** in any quote.
- Customers **sign the quote and pay the deposit on the same screen** (no separate payment link).
- **Turn any milestone into a ready-to-send invoice** in one tap (or ask Sidekick to do it by voice or text).
- Existing users get deposits at **no extra charge** in the latest app update.


When the homeowner signs the quote, it *should be* time to start the real work (the work they’re paying for). But for a lot of pros, collecting the initial payment is a job of its own.


Maybe you create the invoice by hand and send a separate payment link, which can take an hour each time for a job that hasn’t been officially funded yet.


More often than not, you're stuck either waiting on a check while your crew sits idle or fronting the money yourself and hoping the customer doesn’t back out.


**With Topline Pro, the payment schedule is now part of a single flow that starts with the quote.** The customer signs and pays the deposit on one screen, and every payment after that is just one tap away. That way, you can focus more on the work that matters.


[Try Topline Pro Free →](https://www.toplinepro.com/signup)


## **Why quick deposits are crucial for growing your business**


According to[Xero’s latest data](https://www.xero.com/us/media-releases/us-xsbi-march-quarter/) , small businesses are already waiting nearly a month to get paid, with invoices taking an average of 28.8 days to clear. For many pros, that creates a cash flow issue that delays jobs.


Collecting a deposit up front protects your cash flow and covers material costs, so you can start work without delay or putting yourself at risk.


Say you get called to bid on a bigger job (the kind you want more of). It’ll take a few weeks of work, and you'll need to order a lot of materials before you start.


A deposit covers the cost of materials and holds the customer's spot on your calendar. Without it, you either:


- **Wait on cash flow and let the timeline slip.** A late start on a big job can lead to a bad review and limit future bids.
- **Front the cost and bear the risk.** If the job falls through, you may be stuck with materials you can't return, not to mention that if you have cash or credit tied up in one job, you don’t have much available to spend on another.


## **Quotes, deposits, invoices, and payment schedules in one flow**


With Topline Pro, quotes now flow straight into deposits, invoices, and ongoing payments. You can now build your own payment schedule into the quote and move a customer from a signed quote to a down payment in a single tap.


Here's how it works:


### **1. Set the payment schedule up front**


When you edit a quote, you can add a deposit, a milestone, or both, as a percentage or a flat dollar amount. Customers see the full schedule right in the quote, so they know what they're expected to pay and when.


Once you send the quote, the customer can sign and pay the deposit on the same screen, no extra link required.


To start, open any quote and tap **Deposits & Payment Schedule** .


### **2. Send the invoice without extra work**


You can tap once to turn any milestone you already set up into an invoice with the amount, memo, and payment status already filled in.


Check it, edit it if needed, and tap **Send Invoice** . Your customer gets a payment link right away. You can collect payments without keeping a running tab in your head.


### **3. Ask Sidekick to do it**


Gloves on? Hands full? No problem. You can set up a quote, milestone, deposit, or invoice by voice or text with Sidekick, Topline Pro’s AI assistant.


Say "Sidekick, take a $100 deposit," or "Split the job into three payments," or "Send the invoice for the next milestone." Sidekick handles it, so you can get back to work.


[Try Topline Pro Free Today →](https://www.toplinepro.com/signup)


**Already a Topline Pro user?** Deposits and payment schedules are in the latest update, included at no extra charge. Update the app and start using it on your next job.


## **How to handle deposits like a pro**


### **Be upfront**


When asking for money before a job is complete, transparency goes a long way. Most of the time, when a homeowner pushes back on a deposit, it’s a trust issue. Some just want to know what the deposit is for.


Before you ask for any money, put the payment schedule in the quote, so customers can see how much they'll pay and when.


You can also bring it up during your on-site estimate. If a customer asks, "About how much will this run me?" try: "I'll send a formal quote after the inspection. It'll show the deposit amount and the full payment schedule." That way, they know to expect a deposit for the work.


### **Know your state's limits**


Some states cap how much you can collect up front. In California, for example, a home improvement down payment can't exceed $1,000 or 10% of the contract price (whichever is less). Subsequent payments can't exceed the value of the work completed or materials delivered. Maryland allows up to a third of the job price. Check your state's rules before you build a schedule.


### **Send a personal note (then automate the nagging)**


A quick message with the first invoice feels much warmer than sending an invoice and a payment link.


After that, follow-ups are crucial to make sure the customer doesn’t stall. Sending[just two reminder emails can recover 80% of your late invoices](https://trove.works/how-many-invoice-reminders-should-you-send/) , but remembering to send them is half the battle. Topline Pro can automatically send follow-up messages for you.
